pages.name: Speed Bands
pages.html:
The following outlines using vehicles in Spacer.

Speed Bands: Vehicles have speed bands which indicate the top speed of the vehicle.

  • Top speed operation: When using a vehicle at top speed, apply a -1DM for every step above the operator’s Drive (Vehicle) rank.
  • Cruising speed: Vehicles with speed band 3+ have a cruising speed equal to one speed band less than top speed, in which the operator doesn't need to apply any penalties from top Speed operation.
  • Example: Dmitri has Drive (Civilian) 2 and is operating a ground car with speed band 4. The ground car's cruising speed is 3, so he can operate it without a DM penalty at speed 3, but if he pushes the vehicle to speed 4, he will incur -2DM.

pages.name: Vehicle Listings
pages.html:
Vehicle Listings: The following are different basic vehicles for use in a Spacer campaign. Each vehicle is separated into different categories based on the required Drive or Pilot Skill needed to operate it effectively.

  • Cargo: For every one occupant slot, 50kg of cargo can be carried instead.
  • Weapons: Weapons can be added to a vehicle after purchase if the spacer desires to, but civilian vehicles are unarmed by default.
  • Armour: If adding armour to an aircraft, Increase its weight by 0.5T and reduce its speed by 1. An aircraft cannot have armour weight equal to or more than the starting weight of the vehicle.
  • Distance of Operation: This indicates the maximum distance a vehicle can travel without needing to be refuelled.

pages.name: Vehicle Traits
pages.html:
• Air: This vehicle is designed to be flown in the atmosphere of a planet. Those operating vehicles with this trait benefit from using the Pilot (Aircraft) Skill.
  • Archaic: This vehicle is considered a rarity on higher tech worlds, so acquiring them or parts for them is difficult. Apply a -DM equal to the difference between the vehicle's lower tech level and the planet's higher tech level.
  • Civilian: Civilian vehicles are easily available on any world of equal tech level or higher. If searching for civilian vehicles on lower tech worlds or for parts to repair the vehicle, apply the difference between the local tech level and the vehicle's tech level as a -DM.
  • Ascend: This grav vehicle isn't limited by the 6m ceiling of height above a surface, but takes 1 hour per 1km to move vertically. Ascend grav vehicles effectively have VTOL.
  • Grav: This vehicle is operated using the Drive (Grav) Skill.
  • Hover: This vehicle glides across a surface on a cushion of air. This allows the vehicle to travel over land and water at the same speed.
  • Land: This vehicle requires solid ground to be used.
  • Marine: This vehicle is designed for water use only. Those operating vehicles with this trait benefit from using the Marine Skill.
  • Military: This vehicle is only available at military-owned locations and is available for military personnel to use.
  • Industrial: Similar to the Military trait but instead applied for industrial locations and companies or licensed contractors.
  • Open: In the case of any interior hit, roll 1D; a result of 2+ results in the occupants or cargo being hit instead of the system.
  • Sub: This vehicle is capable or designed for underwater functionality.
  • VTOL: This craft can lift and land vertically without needing to use a runway or length of distance for ascending.

Book p.48
